Don't worry — you've actually made real progress. Your line now has full service (5G, excellent signal) and data/roaming on, so the network side is healthy. That means the remaining cause is almost certainly one of two settings on the phone itself.

Please run these two checks on your device and tell me exactly what they say:

I'm looking for two things: whether the APN status shows "Incorrect," and specifically whether the **MMSC URL** is set. The MMSC is the server that handles picture messages — if that field is blank or wrong, MMS will fail even with perfect signal and data.

**2. Check your messaging app permissions** → `check_app_permissions` for "messaging"
I'm looking for whether **storage** and **sms** permissions are granted. Without storage, the app can't attach your photo; without SMS, it can't send at all.

Once you report back:
- If the APN/MMSC is incorrect or blank, I'll have you reset the APN settings and then reboot (the reboot is required for it to take effect).
- If the permissions are missing, I'll have you grant storage and sms to the messaging app.

One quick note: please also confirm **Wi-Fi Calling** is off — since your Wi-Fi is off it likely isn't a factor here, but it can occasionally interfere with MMS if it was enabled earlier.
